subject: Business Models
title: Ford's Assembly Line
description: A quick win: understand Ford's Assembly Line.

hook.text: In 1913, a Model T took 12 hours to build. Henry Ford cut that to 93 minutes.

buildup.text: The assembly line moved the car to the worker instead of the worker to the car.

discovery.text: Ford then doubled wages to $5/day. Workers could now afford the cars they built.

twist.text: Higher wages reduced turnover from 370% to under 16%. Paying more actually cost less.

climax.text: Ford's model created the middle class consumer. Mass production needed mass consumption.

punchline.text: Pay them enough to buy the product. Ford's real genius.

quiz.question: What was Ford's daily wage that revolutionized labor?

details.summary: Henry Ford's moving assembly line in 1913 reduced Model T production time from 12 hours to 93 minutes per car. Combined with the 5-dollar daily wage that attracted the best workers, Ford's system made automobiles affordable for the workers who built them, creating the mass consumer market.
details.whyItMatters: Ford's assembly line did not just transform manufacturing; it created the middle-class consumer economy. By paying workers enough to buy the products they made.
takeaways: The moving assembly line cut Model T production time from 12 hours to 93 minutes
The 5-dollar daily wage was double the industry average and attracted top workers
Mass production made automobiles affordable for ordinary American families

faq.question: How did the moving assembly line change manufacturing economics?
faq.answer: Workers stayed stationary while the car moved to them, eliminating walking time. Each worker performed one specialized task repeatedly. This reduced the skill level required, shortened training time, and dramatically increased output per worker. The cost per car dropped from 850 to 260 dollars.

faq.question: Why did Ford pay workers the unprecedented 5-dollar daily wage?
faq.answer: Assembly line work was monotonous and turnover was 370 percent annually. The 5-dollar wage attracted and retained workers. It also created customers who could afford Model Ts. Ford realized that well-paid workers buying products created a virtuous economic cycle.
